evidence.experimental_conditions: 1% ω-6-hexadecenlactone, vehicle not specified, guinea pigs (6–8 per group), 21 daily open applications to shaved flank, challenge on days 21 and 35, reactions read at 24, 48, and 72 h
evidence.support_text: An open epicutaneous test (OET) was conducted with 1% ω-6-hexadecenlactone (vehicle not specified) in guinea pigs. Induction consisted of 21 daily open applications to the shaved flank of 6–8 guinea pigs per group. Open challenge applications were made on days 21 and 35. Reactions were read at 24, 48 and 72 h. There were no sensitization reactions recorded (Klecak, 1979).

evidence.experimental_conditions: 10% benzyl formate (vehicle not specified); induction with 21 daily open applications at concentrations 100, 30, 10, 3, 1, or 0.3%; open challenge on days 21 and 35; guinea pigs (6-8 per group)
evidence.support_text: Two separate open epicutaneous tests (OET) were conducted with 10% benzyl formate in guinea pigs. Induction consisted of 21 daily open applications at concentrations 100, 30, 10, 3, 1, or 0.3%, and open challenge on days 21 and 35. No reactions were observed (Klecak, 1979, 1985).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Daily applications for 3 weeks to 6–8 guinea pigs with 0.1 mL of phenethyl acetate at concentrations 100%, 30%, 10%, 3%, 1%, or 0.3%; challenge on days 21 and 35 with 0.025 mL of 10% phenethyl acetate; scored at 24, 48, and 72 h
evidence.support_text: In an open epicutaneous test (OET) with phenethyl acetate at various induction concentrations, a challenge concentration of 10% phenethyl acetate was not sensitizing to guinea pigs.

evidence.experimental_conditions: GOHI (SPF) strain albino guinea pigs, weight 330-470 g; induction with 3%, 10%, 30%, or 50% Phytantriol in ethanol, epicutaneous, 5 days/week for 4 weeks; first challenge with 0%, 1%, 3%, 5%, 10% Phytantriol in ethanol; second challenge with 0.1%, 0.3%, 1%, 3%, 5% Phytantriol in ethanol; observations at 24 and 48 h after challenge.
evidence.support_text: In an open epicutaneous test (OET) on GOHI (SPF) strain albino guinea pigs, Phytantriol was tested for skin sensitization potential. Induction phase used ethanol or 3%, 10%, 30%, or 50% Phytantriol in ethanol epicutaneously 5 days/week for 4 weeks. Challenge with 0-10% Phytantriol in ethanol produced sensitization at concentrations of 3% or higher; concentrations ≤1% did not elicit a response. The author concluded that Phytantriol can cause sensitization in guinea pigs at challenge concentrations ≥3%.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pig (outbred male and female, 6-8/group); induction: 0.1 ml of 8% vetiverol on 8 cm²; challenge: 0.025 ml of 8% vetiverol on 2 cm²; vehicle not reported.
evidence.support_text: Open epicutaneous test (OET) was carried out in outbred male and female guinea pigs (6–8/group) with 8% vetiverol (vehicle not reported). Inductions consisted of 0.1 ml of 8% vetiverol applied onto an 8 cm² area. Challenge applications were made with 0.025 ml of test material onto a skin area measuring 2 cm². No sensitization reactions were observed (Klecak, 1985).
